home.subtitle: Play the psychological horror visual novel online, free
home.whatIsP1: The Freak Circus is a psychological horror visual novel from independent developer Garula (Neko Bueno), published on itch.io. It has built a passionate following for its haunting gothic artwork, morally complex characters, and deeply branching narrative set in a mysterious circus appearing only at night. You arrive as a stranger at a remote circus materialized at the edge of a fog-shrouded town. What begins as curiosity quickly becomes entanglement with five performers who have been waiting for someone like you.
home.whatIsP2: You arrive as a stranger at a remote circus materialized at the edge of a fog-shrouded town. What begins as curiosity quickly becomes entanglement. The five performers — Pierrot, Harlequin, Jester, the Ticket Taker, and the Doctor — sense something in you they have been waiting for. Every choice shapes your fate and theirs across two intense days of carnivals, tent shows, and midnight conversations that reveal the circus true nature.
features: Five romanceable characters each with unique story routes and multiple endings
Branching narrative where every choice shifts character affinity and unlocks story branches
Gothic psychological horror atmosphere with original hand-drawn artwork
Official Simplified Chinese language support alongside English
Free to play in your browser or download for Windows, macOS, Linux
home.charactersP: Five performers shape every playthrough of The Freak Circus: Pierrot, Harlequin, Jester, the Ticket Taker, and the Doctor. Each has a unique route, ending set, and relationship arc with the protagonist.
home.howToPlayP1: Playing is simple. The game runs entirely in your browser — no download or installation needed. Click the play button above to launch this visual novel directly on this page. It uses a classic interface: read the story, make choices at key moments, and watch how your decisions shape the narrative across two days of carnivals and tent performances.
home.howToPlayP2: Each playthrough takes 2 to 3 hours. Five main story routes tied to different performers: Pierrot, Harlequin, Jester, the Ticket Taker, and the Doctor. Your first playthrough naturally leads toward one or two characters based on early choices.
home.howToPlayP3: New players should focus on enjoying the atmosphere rather than optimizing for a specific ending. Multiple playthroughs are rewarded — each route reveals new scenes and backstory you cannot see in a single run.

faqItems.q: Is this game free to play?
faqItems.a: Yes. It is completely free to play in your browser on this site. You can also download it for Windows, macOS, and Linux from the official itch.io page. No hidden costs or in-app purchases.

faqItems.q: Do I need to download anything?
faqItems.a: No. It runs directly in your browser. Just click the play button and it loads instantly. No plugins or accounts required.

A single playthrough takes about 2 to 3 hours. To experience all five character routes and endings, expect 10 to 15 hours total across multiple playthroughs. Each playthrough reveals different content.

Yes. The game includes a built-in save system that lets you save at any decision point. You can create multiple save slots to explore different story branches without committing to a single path. Progress is stored locally in your browser.

faqItems.q: What makes this visual novel unique?
faqItems.a: It stands out for its gothic psychological horror atmosphere, morally complex characters, and deeply branching narrative where every choice carries real weight. The hand-drawn art and haunting soundtrack create an immersive experience unlike typical visual novels.
Saves are stored locally in your browser. Download the game from itch.io to transfer save files between devices.

faqItems.q: Is it suitable for all ages?
faqItems.a: No. It is rated 18+ and contains psychological horror, possessive relationships, dark romance, and mature themes.

faqItems.q: What is the difference between routes?
faqItems.a: Each route offers a completely different perspective on the story. Pierrot focuses on psychological dependence and emotional control. Harlequin explores chaos and performance. Jester examines the ethics of entertainment. The Ticket Taker reveals the deepest lore about the circus itself. The Doctor contains the most intimate and unsettling content.
It runs in most modern mobile browsers, though optimized for desktop and tablet for the best experience.

home.storyP1: The Freak Circus begins when you stumble upon a traveling circus. Drawn by an inexplicable pull, you step past the entrance into a world where reality bends. Each performer offers a different perspective on the circus hidden history — Pierrot weeps through his performances but sees everything.
home.storyP2: As night falls, the masks begin to slip. You confront uncomfortable truths about desire, control, and the stories we tell ourselves. The endings range from tender to terrifying, and the game does not judge whichever path you choose. The atmosphere shifts between day and night, with each part revealing different moods and secrets.
tipsList: Take your time reading each scene. Small details often become important later in the story.
Do not reload saves on your first playthrough. Your natural decisions lead to the most meaningful experience.
Play through at least twice — a second run reveals missed dialogue and scenes you cannot see the first time.
Pay close attention to the Ticket Taker. He says more than he appears to say throughout the story.
Each character route has a Good Ending and at least one Bad Ending. The conditions are specific — refer to the walkthrough after your first play.
Use the save system at major decision points to explore alternative paths without losing progress.
home.whyPlayText: The Freak Circus has earned a dedicated following because it offers genuinely difficult choices with real emotional weight. It does not hold your hand or tell you which choice is right. The gothic art style — all hand-drawn illustrations — sets this visual novel apart from typical anime-style titles. The branching narrative tracks over a dozen variables per playthrough, delivering a different experience every time.
home.storyP3: The circus itself is a character. Tents shift positions between visits, carnival games seem to know your thoughts, and performers remember conversations you never had. The experience lingers long after you finish, inviting you back to explore paths you did not take.
home.gameplayP: Gameplay centers on dialogue choices throughout each day. Some choices are timed, adding tension to conversations. Others seem simple but can redirect an entire character route. The game tracks affinity levels with each character, hidden flags for story branches, and cumulative choices that affect the final ending. Even minor interactions can cascade into major consequences later.

characters.title: Characters of The Freak Circus
characters.subtitle: Five extraordinary performers. Five routes. One fate.

list.name: Pierrot
list.description: Controlled, melancholic, and intensely perceptive. Pierrot is the emotional anchor of the circus, performing sorrow for crowds who laugh at his tears. His route is the most psychologically demanding and offers the most lore about the circus's true nature.
list.routeTip: Choose introspective and empathetic dialogue in Day 1. Avoid defiance in Day 2 to unlock the Good Ending.

list.name: Harlequin
list.description: Unpredictable and theatrical, Harlequin masks a turbulent past behind an ever-shifting performance. His relationship with Pierrot is one of the game's central dynamics.
list.routeTip: Select the red balloon in Day 1. Use bold, playful responses during tent encounters.

list.name: Jester
list.description: Jester exists between the other performers, neither fully loyal nor fully antagonistic. His route explores the ethics of entertainment and what it means to make others laugh.
list.routeTip: Jester's route unlocks in Day 2. Respond with humor but avoid direct confrontation.

list.name: Ticket Taker
list.description: The first character you meet. The Ticket Taker controls who enters and who leaves, and has watched everything at this circus for far longer than the others realize.
list.routeTip: Engage directly with every question the Ticket Taker asks. His route requires persistence.

list.name: Doctor
list.description: The Doctor's route is the most recently expanded and contains some of the game's darkest content. He is methodical, intimate, and deeply unsettling.
list.routeTip: The Doctor's content is largely contained to Day 2. Accept his examination scenes to progress his route.

walkthrough.title: The Freak Circus Walkthrough
walkthrough.subtitle: Step-by-step guides for every route, ending, and hidden scene.
walkthrough.spoilerText: This page contains major spoilers for all routes and endings. Play through at least Day 1 before consulting this guide.
walkthrough.day1P1: Day 1 establishes your affinity with each of the five characters through a series of carnival encounters. Your choices in the first 20 minutes determine which routes become available in Day 2.
walkthrough.day1P2: Key branching points in Day 1 include the entrance interaction with the Ticket Taker, the tent choice, and the evening meal conversation.
walkthrough.pierrotP1: Select introspective and empathetic options throughout Day 1. In the tent scene, follow the white cloak. During Day 2, choose understanding over resistance to unlock Pierrot's Good Ending.
walkthrough.pierrotP2: See the full Pierrot route article in our blog.
walkthrough.harlequinP1: Interact with the red balloon during the Day 1 carnival opening. Use bold, playful responses in the main tent. Harlequin's route escalates quickly in Day 2, so embrace the chaos rather than resist it.
